problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<-x}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?

feedback.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4,\,0\le x\le 1}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,,\,0<x<1}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/d60700d57ddc72bb410b3136f546705676f83d23d9071ffe972c5163d11af549.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/75e0132cd3854f18e9ab409b7fd13af3898f78b5174647bf2b33b8438b9228cb.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,0<x<1}.
$$
